title: Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard could be available for Carabao Cup final, says Mikel Arteta
content:
Mikel Arteta says Arsenal’s club captain Martin Odegaard could be in contention for the Carabao Cup final on Sunday.

Odegaard, 27, has not appeared for Arsenal since the north London derby on February 22 due to a knee injury. He now has a matter of days to prove his fitness ahead of the Wembley final against Manchester City.

“We’re really pushing,” Arteta told a press conference on Monday. “He really wants to try to be available, but we’ll have to wait and see in the next few days when he trains with the team how he feels.”

Speaking ahead of Arsenal’s Champions League round of 16 second leg, Arteta confirmed that Odegaard would not be available to face Bayer Leverkusen at the Emirates Stadium. Jurrien Timber, who was withdrawn with an injury during Saturday’s win over Everton, is also out.

Leandro Trossard, however, has returned to training and is expected to make the squad.

Arteta acknowledged that Odegaard could be a helpful role model for Max Dowman, who is following the Norwegian’s path in playing first-team football in his teenage years.

“All the experiences that the players have and they can share and explain, it’s very useful,” said the Arsenal manager.

“Probably he’s going through things that some of us in the past would have been at his age — not many, but Martin is a really good example.”

Before the Carabao Cup final, Arsenal must overcome Leverkusen if they are to reach the Champions League quarter-finals. With the tie finely poised at 1-1 on aggregate, Arteta made clear that his side are well aware of their opponents’ strengths.

“(Leverkusen) are really well coached, a team with a very clear structure, very good individuals,” said Arteta. “Obviously, we are in a stage in the competition that we are in right now, so we know what we have to do and in front of our crowd, with our people, putting all the energy in the world again, hopefully we’re going to do it.”
